relationship_notes: Design work began fall 2008; announcement and first shipments March 2009. Treat FET Dream as CE's first product rather than assuming a larger hidden launch catalog.

Design work began early 2009; Effects Database published the pedal July 27 2010. Uses interchangeable clipping modules, so module states should remain specimen/configuration data rather than separate retail models.
Effects Database published July 31 2010; made for Blue Flame Music shop, establishing a marketed/store relationship worth preserving.
Builder states two years of experimentation preceded the 2010 publication; fully handcrafted discrete overdrive/boost. Do not infer exact 2008 sales date.
Jean-Charles Maillet timeline says spring 2012 brought original pro-grade DIY effect kits; 360 Fuzz is part of the documented five-product catalog. Preserve kit vs completed pedal distinction.
Listed alongside 360 Fuzz in the catalog. Exact first-sale date unresolved.
Listed in early catalog; builder history reaches back to an Acoustic 360 clone pedal made by request in 1995. Preserve antecedent project separately from 2012 product state.
Effects Database weekly overview records the pedal on Aug 2 2010.
Listed in the Aug 2010 weekly overview; later MkI builder videos and model record support continued production. Keep separate from Marshall/JMI Supa Fuzz as a revival/recreation lineage.
Model record published Oct 18 2010. Later evidence shows the builder's MkI lineage and revisions; do not merge into original Sola Sound production.
Published March 20 2012. Handmade germanium Fuzz Face-derived product with internal trim controls; retain as Buffalo retail model rather than original Arbiter identity.
Germanium Fuzz published May 22 2012; V1 limited to 50 units with Matsushita 2SB175, later V2/V3 changed transistor sourcing. Strong generation/specimen evidence.
Published Aug 20 2013; handmade silicon fuzz using selected BC108 transistors with Shape, Fuzz and Level controls.
Published Aug 20 2013; Colorsound Powerboost-derived product with 18V internal headroom from a 9V supply. Keep the Colorsound relationship as lineage, not identity merger.
Published June 16 2014. Described as a heavily reworked Muff-derived overdrive with mixed silicon/germanium implementation and contour control.
NAMM 2013 record; Austin, Texas boutique overdrive with selectable clipping and EQ-shaping options.
ICBM is the original documented version at NAMM 2013; later renamed SCUD Fuzz after a trademark conflict. Preserve both names as successive retail states, not duplicate unrelated pedals.

Published Feb 21 2014 and documented as California-handcrafted analog hybrid spanning boost, overdrive, distortion and fuzz. Treat as an early Vertex dirt anchor; broader Vertex catalog requires later completion.
